cards.title: The medicine drawer is a crime scene
cards.body: Old strips, mystery tablets, a thermometer with a dead battery. Here's what actually belongs in there, so anyone can help in a hurry.

cards.title: Current medicines, in one place
cards.body: Only what the doctor has prescribed right now. Keep each in its original strip or box so the name and expiry stay visible.

cards.title: The latest prescription
cards.body: A paper copy, plus a clear photo on someone's phone. Chemists, doctors and siblings will all ask for it at some point.

cards.title: A simple list on paper
cards.body: Medicine name, strength, timing like 1-0-1, and what it's for. Tape it inside the drawer. Update it after every doctor visit.

cards.title: Basic kit that actually works
cards.body: A working thermometer, a BP machine or sugar meter if the doctor asked for home checks, and a small first aid set. Check batteries monthly.

cards.title: Emergency numbers on top
cards.body: 112, the family doctor, the nearest hospital and two family contacts. Big font. Parents shouldn't need reading glasses in an emergency.

cards.title: What to clear out
cards.body: Expired strips, loose unlabelled tablets and medicines that were stopped. Ask your chemist how to dispose of them instead of leaving them around.

cards.title: A drawer anyone can read
cards.body: If a neighbour had to help Papa at 2am, could they make sense of it in a minute? That's the test.

takeaway: Keep current medicines in original strips, a written list, the latest prescription and emergency numbers. Clear out everything else.
share: Forward to the family group before someone finds 2019's cough syrup in the drawer.
